title: Sources & Methodology
text:
This interactive analytics platform provides real-time, nonpartisan election intelligence, voting logistics, and electoral projections across all 50 U.S. states and Washington, D.C. for the 2026 Midterm Elections.


Our data architecture integrates verified government registries, official election boards, and national demographic databases:

Official State Election Boards:

North Carolina State Board of Elections (NCSBE): Precinct-level and candidate vote counts sourced directly from the NCSBE official general election tabulation files (results_pct_20261103.txt).
Official certification and candidate lists from state Secretaries of State and election departments.

Federal Election Commission (FEC):

Candidate filings, committee registrations, and campaign finance disclosures for U.S. Senate and U.S. House contests.

U.S. Census Bureau:

State population figures from recent decennial and American Community Survey (ACS) updates.
Congressional apportionment figures and state Electoral College allocations (post-2020 apportionment active for 2024–2028).

National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL):

Statutory state voter identification laws, early voting schedules, and primary election calendar benchmarks.






To maintain the highest standards of journalistic integrity and analytical transparency, all data presented on this website is classified under two distinct categories:

Official Results Available: Applied exclusively when ballots have been tabulated and certified by official state election authorities (e.g., North Carolina NCSBE precinct returns).
Consensus Polling / Model Projection: Applied to ongoing races prior to official ballot certification. These benchmarks combine publicly verified nonpartisan polling averages, historical district baselines, and certified candidate filings. Projections and polling are never presented as official vote totals.






Engine: Built with Quarto and modern web standards.
Cartography: High-resolution responsive Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) with individual bounding-box projections.
Visual Analytics: Client-side vector charting powered by Chart.js for responsive, zero-latency state transitions.
Hosting: Static deployment ready for GitHub Pages.


Last Updated: November 13, 2026
